title: Self-hosted Send files cannot be downloaded
body:
## Describe the Bug

Self-hosted Send files cannot be downloaded.

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Create a new send to share a file.
2. Open link to the file.
3. Click download.
4. The button will change to a spinning icon but nothing happens.

## Expected Result

File should download.

## Actual Result

File does not download.

## Screenshots or Videos

N/A

## Environment

- Operating system: Ubuntu 18.04.5 LTS
- Build Version: 1.41.3
- Self Hosted: true
- Environment: Cloud
- Hardware: Hosted VPS

## Additional Context

Doing some digging through various logs led to nothing.
After browsing the bwdata directory I stumbled upon something that may or may not have anything to do with the problem.
In _~/bwdata/core_ I see two directories. One is named _**attachments**_ while the other is named _**attchments**_. The file I uploaded is stored within _attchments_ while the _attachments_ directory is empty. In _~/bwdata/nginx/default.conf_ the location there points to _attachments_.
I see that in server/src/Core/Settings/GlobalSettings.cs on lines 13 and 14 it mentions _attchments_.
I don't know if this is intentional, by design, or a typo.
author: dlrudie

comments.author: c4539
comments.body:
Have you checked the `./bwdata/env/global.override.env` for these entries?

```
globalSettings__attachment__baseDirectory=/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments
globalSettings__attachment__baseUrl=https://vault.example.net/attachments
globalSettings__send__baseDirectory=/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments/send
globalSettings__send__baseUrl=https://vault.example.net/attachments/send
```
That should override the typo you found in `server/src/Core/Settings/GlobalSettings.cs`.

comments.author: JensSpanier
comments.body:
I got it working with these settings:

```
globalSettings__attachment__baseDirectory=/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments
globalSettings__attachment__baseUrl=https://bitwarden.XXXX.de/attachments
globalSettings__send__baseDirectory=/etc/bitwarden/bwdata/core/attachments/send
globalSettings__send__baseUrl=https://bitwarden.XXXX.de/attachments/send
```

Don't change `globalSettings__attachment__baseDirectory` and `globalSettings__send__baseDirectory`. You just need to adjust `globalSettings__attachment__baseUrl` and `globalSettings__send__baseUrl`.

`globalSettings__attachment__baseDirectory` and `globalSettings__send__baseDirectory` are the paths inside the docker container.

So your paths must start with `/etc/bitwarden/core` because this volume gets mapped to `../core` (see `docker-compose.yml`)

comments.author: dlrudie
comments.body:
They don't have to start with /etc/bitwarden/*. In docker-compose.yml it specificies either "../core/attachments" or "/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments". I don't have a /etc/bitwarden at all. Everything is contained within /root/bwdata and the rest of the directories work just fine.

The ../core/attachments is valid on mine. I think my problem comes from the fact that the source has a typo for the directory and it's messing with everything else. The URL's are fine on mine and I don't see any reason to change the baseUrl settings.

If I don't add those four lines, whenever I create a file send it will end up in bwdata/core/attchments with the typo. I can delete the send and it will properly delete the file too. I just can't download it. I've tried renaming bwdata/core/attachments and creating a symlink in its place that points to attchments but it still didn't work.

comments.author: JensSpanier
comments.body:
> In docker-compose.yml it specificies either "../core/attachments" or "/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments".

You are talking about this line in `docker-compose.yml`, right?
`../core/attachments:/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments`

`../core/attachments` is the source path on your host relative to your `docker-compose.yml` (so in your case it's `/root/bwdata/core/attachments`)
`/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments` is the target path inside the docker container

So you do have `/etc/bitwarden`, but only inside your containers (it's like a separate virtual linux host).

The only thing you can change with `globalSettings__attachment__baseDirectory` and `globalSettings__send__baseDirectory` is the path where it gets mounted inside your docker container. Which doesn't make much sense for me. But because there is this typo, you have to set this.

comments.author: dlrudie
comments.body:
Okay, that makes sense on that. I tried setting the /etc/bitwarden/core/attachments and send one in the global override but it still doesn't work for downloads.

As soon as I click the download button I get the same javascript error as in my original screenshot.

"Refused to connect to 'http://localhost:4000/sendfiles//.../...' because it violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "connect-src 'self' wss://site.com https://api.pwnedpasswords.com https://2fa.directory".

comments.author: JensSpanier
comments.body:
I had the same error message. But setting these entries fixed it for me:

```
globalSettings__attachment__baseUrl=https://bitwarden.XXXX.de/attachments
globalSettings__send__baseUrl=https://bitwarden.XXXX.de/attachments/send
```

comments.author: dlrudie
comments.body:
Thanks. That worked now.
So for mine to work it really needed all four of those lines as @c4539 called out.

```

globalSettings__attachment__baseUrl=https://site.com/attachments
globalSettings__send__baseDirectory=/etc/bitwarden/core/attachments/send
globalSettings__send__baseUrl=https://site.com/attachments/send
```

I just got confused about the /etc/bitwarden path and was trying to change it to /root/bwdata instead.

Will these settings be future-proof or if the typo gets fixed in the source will I need to undo these?

Thanks, @c4539 @Virinum

comments.author: JensSpanier
comments.body:
As far as I can tell from looking at the code, you can remove `globalSettings__attachment__baseDirectory` and `globalSettings__send__baseDirectory` once my pull request (#1374) gets merged and the new release is deployed on your server.
But keeping these entries shouldn't have any disadvantages.
